claims.text: Elemental Cr coatings provide adequate corrosion protection for zirconium-alloy cladding in normal subcritical or PWR primary-water conditions.
Elemental Cr coatings on zirconium-alloy cladding can fail during high-temperature steam exposure.
Premature failure of elemental Cr coatings in high-temperature steam is caused by Cr–Zr interdiffusion.
A thin, conformal, nanostructured Al2O3 layer can be deposited between a zirconium-alloy substrate and an elemental Cr coating.
The proposed Al2O3 interlayer will reduce Cr–Zr interdiffusion.
The proposed Al2O3 interlayer will improve oxidation resistance in both PWR primary water and high-temperature steam.
A dense Al2O3 interlayer will remain stable in the proposed service environments.
The Al2O3 interlayer will impede atomic transport between the Cr coating and zirconium alloy.
The Al2O3 interlayer will promote formation of protective oxide scales during high-temperature exposure.
Al2O3 is sufficiently thermodynamically stable and oxidation resistant to function as a physical and chemical diffusion barrier in this coating system.
Limiting Cr and Zr transport will preserve Cr-coating integrity and maintain corrosion and oxidation protection.
Relative to Cr coating alone, the modified coating will have lower interfacial interdiffusion, better oxidation resistance, and greater overall durability.
High-temperature steam oxidation is a critical performance concern for accident-tolerant zirconium-alloy cladding.
The proposed system is applicable to accident-relevant steam exposures at approximately 800–1000 °C and up to approximately 1000 °C.
The proposed system is applicable over both routine-service exposure times and transient accident exposure times.
The optimal Al2O3 thickness and processing conditions, and its long-term behavior under irradiation and thermal cycling, remain unquantified.
Failure to obtain statistically significant improvements in interdiffusion, oxidation resistance, and coating integrity relative to the Cr-only control would falsify the proposed intervention.
